en.title: S&P 500 put prices quadruple at 6,000

beats.say: S&P 500 put options on the 6,000 strike quadrupled from 7 to 27 points.
The surge occurred during a rapid 4.4% index correction.
Protective contracts down at the 5,500 strike jumped to nearly 15 points.
Implied volatility on deep crash puts climbed straight to 62%, signaling structural fear.
Expensive downside insurance demonstrates that market participants are not treating this as routine profit-taking.
Elevated option pricing leaves the door open to additional volatility spikes.
Keep tracking option skew. Follow for tomorrow's update.

en.title: VWCE drops 7.4%: protective put advantage

beats.say: An unprotected VWCE portfolio lost 7.4%, while a hedged account gained 0.2%.
The broad global ETF retreated alongside the sudden drop in US equities.
Strategic put options completely erased downside volatility over the exact same period.
Insurance must be established during low-volatility regimes when contract pricing is cheap.
Purchasing downside protection during panics results in paying peak premiums.
Structure hedges before drawdowns begin. Follow for tomorrow's update.
